verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '5G refers to the utilization of fifth-generation (5G) wireless technology.'; R2: '5G is the 5th generation mobile network.'; R5: '5G is the fifth generation of cellular networks.'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly define 5G as the fifth generation mobile/cellular network.

verifications.claim: 5G offers speeds up to 100x faster than 4G.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'Up to 100 times faster than 4G'; R7: 'Up to 100x faster than 4G'; R2: '5G can be significantly faster than 4G, delivering up to 20 Gigabits-per-second (Gbps) peak data rates' (implying ~100x peak vs 4G).
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state 5G is up to 100x faster than 4G.

verifications.claim: Key components of 5G include 5G New Radio (spectrum) and a cloud-native Core.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R9: '5G New Radio (NR) and Radio Access Network (RAN)' and 'cloud-native 5GC'; R2: '5G NR air interface'; R10: '5G New Radio (5G NR)' and '5G Next Generation Core'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources identify 5G NR (associated with spectrum/air interface) and cloud-native core as key components of 5G architecture.

verifications.claim: 5G delivers up to 20 Gbps peak data rates.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'delivering up to 20 Gigabits-per-second (Gbps) peak data rates'; R4: 'peak download speeds of up to 20 Gbps'; R5: 'peak data download rates up to 20Gbps'.
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm 20 Gbps peak data rates for 5G.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'a 10x decrease in end-to-end latency down to 1ms'; R4: 'ultra-low latency of 1-2 milliseconds'; R5: 'Latency (shortest delay time) 1 millisecond'; R7: 'super-low, 1ms latency'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently state 5G latency around 1 ms.

verifications.claim: 5G NR operates on both low/mid-bands (sub-7 GHz) and high-frequency bands (mmWave, >24 GHz).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'lower bands (e.g., sub-6 GHz) as well as mmWave (e.g., 24 GHz and up)'; R5: 'Mid-band 5G (1GHz to 6GHz)' 'High-band 5G (24.25GHz to 86GHz)'; R10: 'Sub-6 5G low- and mid-bands' and 'millimeter wave (mmWaves) high-band'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly describe 5G NR/spectrum bands matching low/mid (sub-6/7 GHz) and mmWave (>24 GHz).

verifications.claim: 5G Core (5GC) is a cloud-native, service-based architecture.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R9: '5GC is built on a Service-Based Architecture (SBA), implementing IT network principles and a cloud-native design.'
verifications.reasoning: R9 explicitly describes 5GC as cloud-native and service-based.
